gaps.sentence: Despite the pressure, the surgeon ___ calm throughout the operation.
gaps.explanation: keep calm (or stay calm) means to remain calm; the past tense is needed here.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: Local residents are deeply ___ about the new motorway plan.
gaps.explanation: deeply concerned is the standard collocation meaning very worried; the other adjectives do not collocate with 'deeply'.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ your seats; the performance is about to begin.
gaps.explanation: take your seats is the formal way of asking people to sit down.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her a compliment on her new hairstyle.
gaps.explanation: pay somebody a compliment is the fixed collocation for praising someone.

gaps.sentence: We should ___ an effort to arrive on time.
gaps.explanation: make an effort is the fixed collocation meaning to try hard.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.
